910.name: Megalithic Temples and Prehistoric Malta
910.description: Malta's extraordinary prehistoric period, home to the oldest freestanding structures in the world — megalithic temples predating the Egyptian pyramids and Stonehenge — and the mysterious collapse of the temple-building civilization.

sub_clusters.name: First Settlers and Temple Builders
sub_clusters.description: The arrival of Neolithic settlers from Sicily, the construction of the Ġgantija, Ħaġar Qim, Mnajdra, and Tarxien temples (the oldest freestanding structures on Earth), the Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum, and the mysterious collapse of the temple period.
key_events: Construction of Ġgantija temples on Gozo — world's oldest freestanding structures (c. 3600 BC)
Construction of Ħaġar Qim and Mnajdra temple complexes (c. 3200 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Bronze Age and Phoenician Arrival
sub_clusters.description: The post-temple Bronze Age period, the arrival of Phoenician traders and colonists who established Malta as a crucial Mediterranean waypoint, and the origins of Malta's Semitic linguistic heritage.

910.name: Carthaginian and Roman Malta
910.description: Malta under Carthaginian and then Roman control, St. Paul's legendary shipwreck and the Christianization of the islands, and Malta's role in Mediterranean trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Carthaginian Rule
sub_clusters.description: Malta as a Carthaginian naval base and colony, Punic-Phoenician cultural influence, and the islands' strategic importance in the wars between Carthage and the Greek city-states.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Malta and St. Paul's Shipwreck
sub_clusters.description: Malta's incorporation into the Roman Republic after the Second Punic War, the legendary shipwreck of the Apostle Paul in 60 AD (Acts 28), and the early Christianization of the Maltese islands.
key_events: Legendary shipwreck of the Apostle Paul on Malta (60 AD)

920.name: Arab, Norman, and Medieval Malta
920.description: Byzantine Malta, the transformative Arab period that shaped the Maltese language, the Norman conquest, and the succession of feudal rulers leading to the arrival of the Knights Hospitaller.

sub_clusters.name: Byzantine and Arab Malta
sub_clusters.description: Malta under Byzantine rule, the Arab conquest (870 AD), the profound Arabic influence on the Maltese language, Islamic cultural contributions, and the Norman reconquest by Count Roger I of Sicily.
key_events: Arab conquest of Malta — origins of the Maltese language's Semitic roots (870 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Norman and Medieval Feudal Rule
sub_clusters.description: Malta under Norman, Swabian, Angevin, and Aragonese rulers as part of the Kingdom of Sicily, the development of the Maltese nobility, and the depopulation and re-settlement of the islands.

930.name: Knights Hospitaller and the Great Siege
930.description: The Order of St. John's (Knights Hospitaller) rule of Malta, the legendary Great Siege of 1565 against the Ottoman Empire, the construction of Valletta, and Malta's golden age as a bastion of Christendom.

sub_clusters.name: Arrival of the Knights (1530)
sub_clusters.description: Emperor Charles V's grant of Malta to the Order of St. John after their expulsion from Rhodes, the Knights' fortification of the islands, and the buildup to the Ottoman invasion.

sub_clusters.name: Great Siege of Malta (1565)
sub_clusters.description: The epic four-month Ottoman siege of Malta under Suleiman the Magnificent, the heroic defense led by Grand Master Jean de Valette, and the siege's significance in halting Ottoman expansion in the western Mediterranean.
key_events: Great Siege of Malta — Knights Hospitaller repel massive Ottoman invasion (May–September 1565)

sub_clusters.name: Construction of Valletta and Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The construction of Valletta as a planned fortified city named after Grand Master de Valette, the flourishing of Baroque art and architecture, Caravaggio's stay in Malta, and the gradual decline of the Order.

940.name: Napoleon and British Colonial Malta
940.description: Napoleon's seizure of Malta, the Maltese uprising and British intervention, the establishment of the British Crown Colony, and Malta's development as a vital Royal Navy base in the Mediterranean.

sub_clusters.name: French Occupation and Maltese Revolt
sub_clusters.description: Napoleon's bloodless seizure of Malta from the Knights in 1798, his looting of treasures, the Maltese popular uprising, and the British naval blockade that expelled the French.
key_events: Napoleon seizes Malta from the Knights Hospitaller en route to Egypt (June 1798)

sub_clusters.name: British Crown Colony
sub_clusters.description: Malta as a British Crown Colony, its strategic importance as a Mediterranean naval base, the language question (Italian vs. Maltese vs. English), constitutional development, and the growth of Maltese national identity.

950.name: WWII George Cross and Independence
950.description: Malta's heroic role in WWII as the most bombed place on Earth, the award of the George Cross, and the path to independence and republic status.

sub_clusters.name: WWII Siege and George Cross
sub_clusters.description: Malta's Second Great Siege during WWII: relentless Axis bombing (the most bombed place in WWII), near-starvation, Operation Pedestal convoy, and King George VI's unprecedented award of the George Cross to the entire island.
key_events: King George VI awards the George Cross to the island of Malta for heroism (April 1942)
Operation Pedestal relief convoy reaches besieged Malta (August 1942)

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Republic
sub_clusters.description: Post-war reconstruction, the debate over integration with Britain vs. independence, Malta's independence (September 21, 1964), the declaration of the Republic (1974), and the closure of the British military base (1979).

960.name: EU Membership and Contemporary Malta
960.description: Malta's transformation from a post-colonial economy to an EU member state, the financial services and iGaming boom, and the governance challenges exposed by the Panama Papers and the Caruana Galizia assassination.

sub_clusters.name: EU Accession and Economic Transformation
sub_clusters.description: Malta's economic diversification from naval dockyard dependency, the contentious EU membership referendum (2003), EU accession (May 2004), euro adoption (2008), and the pivot to financial services, tourism, and iGaming.

sub_clusters.name: Governance Crises and Press Freedom
sub_clusters.description: The Panama Papers revelations implicating Maltese officials, the assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia (October 2017), the resulting political crisis, and Malta's ongoing struggle with rule-of-law challenges.
key_events: Assassination of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia by car bomb (October 16, 2017)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
